claim: Channel 7 (kChannelLevelStart) is sent once at the end of trInit, as the level loads, before the player can act. Whatever listens on rx 7 changes before play begins, or a moment after through a relay: E1M1's casket (s30) opens on channel 102 from closet switch sprite 51, which listens on rx 7 and sends when it returns 0.6 s later. A reachability reader that treats it as a player action finds 2 of E1M1's 155 sectors.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/triggers.cpp:2316 (trInit: evSend(0, 0, kChannelLevelStart, kCmdOn, ...)); trInit is called at blood.cpp:800 (StartLevel); eventq.h:33 kChannelLevelStart = 7.
E1M1 sprite 51: type 20, rx 7, tx 102, trigger_off, wait_time 6, in closet s31; s30 (type 614) is rx 102 (python -m tools.catalog record E1M1 sector 30; rechecked 2026-11-26)
bloodmap/conditional.py:323-331 (level_start_closure) gives the 2 of 155 sectors a frontier finds without the closure; counted when it was written, not recounted 2026-11-26
use: Use rx 7 to start machines that run from the outset (crushers, belts); close the level-start closure before reading reachability.
